OPDA · Local exploration · 12 September 2026

From evidence to shared meaning

Twenty distinct visual treatments of one process. Wide artwork, one image per row. Every label and arrow is generated inside the image. The homepage remains unchanged.

Subscription gallery · Open the other gallery

20 / 20 images generated. Built-in subscription image tool; no model, quality or resolution selector is exposed. Effective model is unverified. Both routes receive the same twenty base prompts, including a wide 1280 × 512 target. The API diorama includes one targeted arrow correction; its first attempt is retained. Subscription previews are fresh generations. These are route comparisons, not a verified comparison of specific model versions.

Required process: Source material → Prepare candidate → Publish candidate → Working-group review → Collect feedback → Prepare candidate. A separate consensus exit runs from Working-group review → Draft standard. A draft is not ratified or adopted.

Adversarial prompt review and changes
Failure in the earlier briefsWhy it mattersRevised prompt
“Visible feedback loop” without attachment pointsAllows reversed arrows and review-to-prepare shortcutsSix enumerated edges, explicit entry/exit sides, arrowhead destinations and node degree checks
“Not production art” alongside exact process requirementsWeakens the priority of semantic accuracyRelationships and words take priority over decoration
Style label appended to a generic box templateDifferent media collapse into the same clip-art layoutMaterial, edge character, light, depth and visual form specified for each treatment
Many overlapping print and paper combinationsInflates the count without testing distinct choicesTwenty deliberate treatments; technique and composition type labelled separately
Generic clay description for the marketing referenceMisses architectural precision and realistic miniature peopleActual property-technology image supplied for the diorama; its role is style only
3:2 composition and two-column displayCramped loop and small letteringWide 2.5:1 composition requested; single-column comparison
Texture or physical objects compete with text and arrowsDestinations become ambiguousClean label areas, reserved connector space and consistent arrow geometry

Acceptance checks: six unique headings; six correct directed edges; three exact arrow labels; no invented approval; readable text; unclipped wide composition; visible distinction between styles. The semantic layout is held constant; the material and representation vary.

Model and output provenance

The native OpenAI API recognises the requested Sunburst model ID, and the API requests explicitly use it. The subscription tool exposes no model selector. Original files from both routes record gpt-image version 2.0 in C2PA softwareAgent; this has not been proven to identify the effective model. Metadata was parsed, not cryptographically verified. All 40 outputs are 1983 × 793; gallery renditions are reduced proportionally to 1280 pixels wide. Original output bytes and prompt hashes are retained. API quality was requested as high; subscription quality is automatic and unreported.

01 / Photographed miniature

Architectural miniature diorama

Original output: 1983 × 793 pixels. Gallery rendition: at most 1280 pixels wide.

Compare this style on the other route

Build a continuous architecturally precise clay-and-card tabletop maquette, oblique elevated camera with all stations clearly visible. Realistic miniature adults, matte card workbenches, finely constructed document objects, shallow cutaway structures, physical violet arrow connectors with sculpted arrowheads and a gold draft exit. Soft studio light, contact shadows, deep focus. Serious professional model-making, not rounded toy icons. Reference image 1, when supplied, defines materials, photographic realism and scale only; replace its entire scene and connections with the six-station brief.

Review: Six headings, six directed edges and three arrow labels checked. Miniature architectural stages match the reference technique; additional plants and tiny crests are decorative deviations.

Closest to the requested property-technology image; risk: physical connectors may hide arrowheads.

Exact image prompt
Use case: infographic-diagram. Purpose: help property-data stakeholders understand how evidence becomes a reviewed draft through publication, human review and revision.
Create ONE complete wide landscape illustration, target 1280 x 512 pixels, aspect ratio 2.5:1. Render all artwork, labels and arrows yourself in the specified medium.
LAYOUT: six distinct stations with clear boundaries and generous connecting space. Centres as percentages of canvas: Source material (10,52), Prepare candidate (33,52), Working-group review (67,52), Draft standard (90,52), Collect feedback (50,18), Publish candidate (50,83). Each station at most 16% of canvas width and 25% of height. Keep at least 3% outer margin. The upper and lower stations are part of the loop, not extra rows in a linear sequence.
SUBJECTS: source = authorised evidence folios; prepare = practitioner revising a candidate sheet; publish = an open document portfolio displayed for others; review = two adult practitioners examining the same sheet; feedback = response slips gathered into a distinct tray; draft = a bound working manuscript without approval seals.
EXACT LABELS, each once, in crisp large dark sans-serif lettering on clean paper plaques integrated into the artwork: "Source material", "Prepare candidate", "Publish candidate", "Working-group review", "Collect feedback", "Draft standard". Two-line labels are allowed. No body copy, numbers, title, logo or other lettering except the three arrow labels below.
EXACTLY SIX DIRECTED ARROWS, one arrowhead at each destination:
1. Source material RIGHT edge to Prepare candidate LEFT edge, pointing RIGHT. Label "Initial intake".
2. Prepare candidate BOTTOM edge to Publish candidate LEFT edge, travelling down then right, arrowhead pointing into Publish candidate.
3. Publish candidate RIGHT edge to Working-group review BOTTOM edge, travelling right then up, arrowhead pointing UP into review.
4. Working-group review TOP edge to Collect feedback RIGHT edge, travelling up then left, arrowhead pointing LEFT into feedback. Label "Changes requested".
5. Collect feedback LEFT edge to Prepare candidate TOP edge, travelling left then down, arrowhead pointing DOWN into preparation.
6. Working-group review RIGHT edge to Draft standard LEFT edge, pointing RIGHT. Label "Consensus reached".
Arrows 1-5 violet; arrow 6 gold with dark outline for contrast. Use consistent shaft thickness and arrowhead size. Keep each connector visually continuous and separated from text, objects and other arrows. Leave visible space at every arrowhead so its destination is unambiguous. No other lines resembling connections. Source has no incoming arrow. Draft has no outgoing arrow. Review has two outgoing arrows; preparation has two incoming arrows. The draft is reviewed, not ratified or adopted.
PALETTE: off-white #F9F9F9, deep purple #231F2F, teal #0E8478, violet #6C5BD4. Gold #FEC92B reserved for the consensus exit and draft emphasis. Make labels readable at the small preview size. Prioritise the six relationships and exact words over decorative detail.

STYLE AND FORM: Build a continuous architecturally precise clay-and-card tabletop maquette, oblique elevated camera with all stations clearly visible. Realistic miniature adults, matte card workbenches, finely constructed document objects, shallow cutaway structures, physical violet arrow connectors with sculpted arrowheads and a gold draft exit. Soft studio light, contact shadows, deep focus. Serious professional model-making, not rounded toy icons. Reference image 1, when supplied, defines materials, photographic realism and scale only; replace its entire scene and connections with the six-station brief.
02 / Painted editorial

Translucent watercolour

Original output: 1983 × 793 pixels. Gallery rendition: at most 1280 pixels wide.

Compare this style on the other route

Paint small editorial scenes in translucent washes with granulation, pigment pooling and lost edges. Preserve white paper highlights. Thin purple ink for structures and legible labels. Keep washes within subject areas so connectors retain clear silhouettes. Quiet, humane and observational.

Review: Six headings, six directed edges and three arrow labels checked. Wash texture is visible; extra backgrounds and a crest add detail beyond the brief.

Warm and approachable; risk: pale arrows or muddy lettering.

Emphasises human judgement; risk: loose marks becoming arrow-like.

Sequential ink narrative

Compose six shallow ink narrative panels at the specified six station positions. A recurring candidate document visibly progresses through scenes. Shows handoffs clearly; risk: conventional reading order overriding the loop.

Research sources and method

OpenAI guidance informs prompt structure, reference roles and targeted editing. Printmaking sources inform visual material distinctions. The twenty recipes are original design proposals, not an official model style catalogue. No claim of independent multi-agent review is made.
